nodes.question: What are the two main objectives of the study mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The two main objectives are to investigate the current state of knowledge on the evaluation of the environmental sustainability of EHDs and to identify research gaps in environmental impact evaluation studies.
nodes.paragraph: There is no one-size-fits-all solution to mitigate the envi- ronmental burden of EHDs. Solutions such as eco-design strategies, replacing single-use with reusable EHDs, circu- lar economy strategies, and proper treatment and disposal could enhance the overall sustainability of the healthcare industry. However, the perceived environmental benefits of these strategies are not yet fully understood, nor is the effect on environmental sustainability when considering direct and indirect impacts. To address the above-mentioned shortcom- ings, this study focuses on two objectives: (1) to investi- gate the current state of knowledge on the evaluation of the environmental sustainability of EHDs and (2) to identify research gaps in environmental impact evaluation studies and make recommendations using LCA perspective as the backbone. 2 Methodology This section starts with a brief description of the search strategy used to identify and select eligible studies on the environmental sustainability assessment of EHDs. Subse- quently, the method for extracting data and analysing infor - mation from the selected studies is described. 2.1 Literature search strategy The literature search followed a structured procedure involv - ing the following steps: (i) identifying the databases and search terms, (ii) screening articles, (iii) categorising the selected articles, and (iv) synthesising and analysing the articles.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Product life-cycle analysis|Environmental impact assessment_qna_001
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What methods were specified for the quantitative environmental assessment in the study selection?
nodes.answer: The specified methodologies for quantitative environmental assessment were LCA (Life Cycle Assessment) and footprint method.
nodes.paragraph: A total of 42 studies were selected for full article screening. During the full article screening, each study was assessed individually for relevance to the literature search theme. At this stage, studies were excluded if they did not report original research (i.e. literature review studies). We also excluded studies that did not use quantitative environmental assessment methodologies (i.e. LCA and footprint method). It is important to note that relevant studies mentioned in literature review studies had already been identified dur - ing the screening process and no additional studies were discovered. Also, studies were excluded if the healthcare devices covered were not electronic. The full-text screen- ing ultimately resulted in a selection of fourteen studies. Furthermore, the reference lists of the included articles were sought out to identify additional articles that fit within the scope of the research. After abstract and/or full-text screen- ing of the studies from the reference list, three studies were selected, resulting in a final total of 17 studies included in the analysis. The entire search strategy is depicted in Fig. 1. 2.3 Extraction of information and in depth analysis Extraction of information from the 17 selected studies was performed according to predetermined criteria.

nodes.question: Why is collecting primary activity data essential for environmental impact assessments?
nodes.answer: Collecting primary activity data such as waste loss, energy consumption, water usage, and chemicals inventory is essential for environmental impact assessments to enhance the representativity of the evaluation.

nodes.question: How does Waste Flow Mapping (WFM) enhance Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)?
nodes.answer: Waste Flow Mapping (WFM) enhances EIA by providing detailed information about waste streams, enabling a thorough assessment of the environmental impact. This integration helps companies identify specific waste streams for improvement and promotes sustainability in product life cycles.
